sections.title: Overview
sections.text:
17.1 Overview
There are many instances in QM for which EWS can come in handy, depending on
what’s important to your business. In this chapter, you’ll learn how easy and intuitive
it is to set up EWS by following the steps in logical and sequential order. If the business
requirements change at any time, you can make changes or even delete EWS that
you’ve set up.
Some examples of where you can use EWS are as follows:
 When quality specifications of an important raw material are out by more than 3%
 When the supplier repeatedly fails to deliver acceptable quality raw material
 When a supplier continues to make late deliveries of critical components
 When you record production scrap at greater than 5% of total production
 When sales figures show a decreasing trend for a high-running, high-profit item for
the past three months
 When inventory of precious metal exceeds a certain value

17 Early Warning System
756
In any of these situations, you can configure EWS to the individual exception so that
you’ll receive alerts and can react immediately. While you can set up EWS in any logis-
tics area, we’ll use an example from QM. The relevant information structures available
for QM are listed in Table 17.1.
Note
When EWS is set up for any logistics area, the relevant information structures are auto-
matically made available by the SAP S/4HANA system. For example, if EWS is set up in
production planning (PP), all PP-related information structures become available.

ture from Table 17.1, followed by the characteristics and key figures. The requirements

of each key figure need to be defined next; then, finally, you also define the follow-up
processing. In summary, the following are the required steps:
1. Create an exception.
2. Group the exceptions.
3. Create a periodic analysis.
Note
If there are several exceptions to the same information structure, they can be com-
bined to create a group exception, which is a list of individual exceptions. Like the first
step, the follow-up processing for this step involves determining whether an email
alert to an individual suffices or if it should be communicated to the entire distribution
list.
The third and final step is periodic analysis, in which you define the frequency with
which the system monitors the exceptions and issues alerts. Now let’s discuss the first
step of the process: creating an exception.

sections.title: Create Exceptions
sections.text:
17.2.1 Create Exceptions
An exception is important data that you want to monitor from a business point of view.
The sequence of steps in creating an exception is as follows:
1. Choose characteristics.
2. Define the key figures.
3. Define the characteristics values.
4. Choose requirements.
5. Define the requirements.
6. Define the follow-up processing.
For this example, you’ll create an exception in QM, Z015, using the information struc-
ture S068 (supplier statistics). In exception Z015, you’ll specify that the system should
issue an alert whenever material QM003 has a rejected quantity greater than 50 PC. If
the system records an exception in the SAP S/4HANA system, it should be highlighted
with the color red; the system also should give a popup message and send an email
alert to your SAP inbox.
Use menu path Logistics  Logistics Controlling  QM Information System  Early Warn-
ing System  Exception  Create or Transaction MC=Q to set up the exception (see Figure
17.1).

17 Early Warning System
758
Figure 17.1 Characteristics Setup in EWS
Follow this step-by-step process for creating exception Z015:
1. Enter Exception “Z015”, a short description, and Info Structure “S068”. Choose Char-
acteristics (info structure S068 corresponds to supplier statistics) located on the top
menu bar of the main screen.
2. At the bottom of the screen, click Choose characteristics to select the characteristics
for which you want to activate EWS.
3. In the popup screen that appears, select Material and move it to the left column by
clicking Choose, and then choose Execute.
4. For each characteristic in Figure 17.1, provide the corresponding value or a range
from which to choose. Choose the characteristic Material, and select Charact. values
at the top.
5. In the popup window that appears, enter the desired value or range for which the
system should monitor EWS (Figure 17.2). For this example, enter “QM003” for Mate-
rial, and choose Copy.
Note
You can also give a range of materials for EWS to monitor by filling out both the From
and To fields in Figure 17.2. Alternatively, leaving these fields blank means that EWS
considers all materials in the alert.
© 

759
17.2 Set Up Early Warning System
Figure 17.2 Characteristics Value for Material QM003
Now that the value for the characteristic material is defined, the next step is to define
the requirements—that is, the information that you need EWS to monitor in day-to-
day business processes. Choose Requirements back in Figure 17.1 to define require-
ments for the material. For this example, choose one key figure for the material (Figure
17.3) by following these steps:
1. On the Create Exception: Requirements screen, click on Choose key figures, and
from the subsequent popup screen, select the key figures that will form the basis of
your EWS alerts. For this example, select the Rejected quantity key figure by moving
it from the right side to the left side with Choose.
2. Choose Continue.
3. Define the Period to analyze fields, which stipulate the past and future periods for
which EWS must evaluate deviations. By defining Previous periods as “12”, you stip-
ulate that all key figures for the past 12 months that meet the conditions must be
considered during evaluation.
4. After selecting the key figures, choose Define requirement to specify the limits or
other details that form the basis for EWS alerts. The requirement has to be defined
for each key figure. The options available are Threshold val. anal., which requires a
value to be specified, or Trend analysis, which is used to monitor positive or negative
trends and requires you to specify the percentage of deviation in the trend. The third
option is a comparison between planned and actual value of a key figure that can
then be analyzed for deviation.

17 Early Warning System
760
Figure 17.3 Key Figures for EWS
5. For the Rejected quantity key figure, shown in Figure 17.4, place the cursor on the key
figure and double-click it; alternatively, you can choose Define requirement. A
popup appears.
Figure 17.4 Requirements for Key Figures
© 

761
17.2 Set Up Early Warning System
6. In the popup window, select the Threshold val. anal. radio button, and click the Con-
tinue button. In the next popup window that appears, enter “=> 50”, and then choose
Continue. This step stipulates that you want to monitor the material quantity when
the rejected quantity equal to or exceeds 50 PC.
Note
All other standard operands, such as less than, greater than, equal to, and not equal to,
are available for use when setting threshold values.
The next step in defining an exception is to define the follow-up processing—that is,
when and how EWS informs you that an exception has occurred. For this example,
choose Follow-Up Processing, shown in the top-menu bar of Figure 17.4, to bring up the
screen shown in Figure 17.5.
Figure 17.5 Follow-Up Processing
Here, we’ve specified that whenever the exception Z015 occurs, the details are to be
marked in red and sent as a table to the entered mail recipient. Further, the same needs
to be communicated by email to the corresponding SAP inbox.

17 Early Warning System
762
Tips and Tricks
Select both the Active for std [standard] analysis and Active for periodic analysis
checkboxes in Figure 17.5; these subsequently will be checked whenever you run analy-
sis reports in EWS.

sections.title: Group Exceptions
sections.text:
17.2.2 Group Exceptions
If you want to monitor more than one exception from the same information structure
in EWS, you should group them together in exception groups for ease of reporting. For
example, if the same material’s scrap is monitored with its upper tolerance limit marked
with the color red and its lower tolerance limit marked with the color yellow, then
grouping these two different exceptions provides details in one list or report in EWS.
Let’s clarify this further. You define that whenever the material scrap is exceeded by 10%
(upper tolerance limit), the system highlights it in red in EWS. When the material scrap
is less than 10% (lower tolerance limit), the system highlights it in yellow in EWS. If no
such requirement exists, then you don’t need to define the exception grouping.
Note
For this example, exception grouping isn’t used. However, the concepts and other
details covered in this chapter are sufficient for a user to quickly set up exception
grouping. Exception grouping is found in the same menu path as EWS.

sections.title: Set Up Periodic Analysis
sections.text:
17.2.3 Set Up Periodic Analysis
Now that the exceptions have been defined, the last step in setting up EWS is to define
the frequency with which the system should alert the person who set up EWS (e.g.,
every eight hours, daily, once a week, or once a month). For this example, we need to set
up periodic analysis for exception Z015 by setting up the variant and defining the fre-
quency of the analysis.
To do so, follow menu path Logistics  Logistics Controlling  QM Information System 
Early Warning System  Periodic Analysis  Area to Analyze  Create or use Transaction
MC=W to get to the Periodic Analysis screen (see Figure 17.6 1). Then, follow these
steps:
1. Enter the Exception for periodic analysis, which is “Z015”, and choose Create.
2. A popup window appears asking for the name of the variant to create. Define “Z015”
as the variant. Choose Create in the popup window to open the Edit Variants:
Change Screen Assignment screen.
3. Define this variant as applicable for the individual screens (For Indiv. Selection
Screens), which means that the parameters of variant Z015 and material QM003 are
© 

763
17.2 Set Up Early Warning System
automatically available for selection on the EWS screen for info structure S068 and
number 1710 2. If you choose the For All Selection Screens radio button, then these
parameters are available for all the different screens of EWS by default.
4. Choose Continue to open the Maintain Variant screen. You can define the initial
screen parameters for your variant here. For this example, define that the system
should automatically select material QM003 and make it available as default.
Figure 17.6 Setting Up Periodic Analysis
After defining the parameters, choose Attributes to get to the screen shown in Figure
17.7, where you can provide a meaningful description of the variant. This description is
communicated whenever EWS needs to alert an exception. An example of a meaning-
ful description is “Production-based material is out of specification,” which immedi-
ately alerts the concerned person to respond. Contrast this with a more generic and
vague description, such as “QM specs are out.” This approach also helps if the same
alert is sent to many people in the form of a distribution list. For this example, enter the
Description “Suppliers’ Rejections”. Finally, click Save to save the periodic analysis.

17 Early Warning System
764
A message appears to confirm that variant Z015 is saved with all the values on the selec-
tion screen.
Figure 17.7 Maintain Variants in EWS

sections.title: Schedule Early Warning System
sections.text:
17.3 Schedule Early Warning System
You now need to define the scheduling information on exception Z015 to determine
how frequently the system should analyze it for potential exceptions. Use SAP menu
path Logistics  Logistics Controlling  QM Information System  Early Warning System 
Periodic Analysis  Schedule or Transaction MC=Z to bring up the initial screen for
scheduling exception Z015 (Figure 17.8). After defining exception Z015, choose Schedule
to schedule the analysis frequency of your exceptions.
Figure 17.8 shows two options: to either schedule the analysis of the exception group
immediately or define it as a periodic job and then define the period values. Choose
Other period, then enter “1” in the Minute(s) field in the resulting popup.
The option to schedule the job immediately ensures that any new exception is imme-
diately reported. However, if the Date/Time is used, for example, then exception mon-
itoring and reporting start on that specified date and time only, as a scheduled job. The
second option of scheduling a periodic job helps ensure that system resources aren’t
unduly overburdened.
© 

765
17.3 Schedule Early Warning System
Figure 17.8 Define Schedule Details for EWS
Tips and Tricks
The scheduling frequency should be practical, as well as have a reasonable cadence—
for example, daily. Under the Daily scheduling option, all exceptions for the entire day
are consolidated into one issued alert. This allows the person who set up the alert to
attend to all exceptions in one sitting.
Choose Save to save the scheduling details. Then, a message appears to confirm that
the background job for exception Z015 has been successfully planned.
This ends our discussion on how to set up EWS. The next section shows how EWS works
in the system when the user performs day-to-day business functions, and how the sys-
tem alerts the user who sets up EWS when an exception occurs. The business users can
continue to perform and report their daily activities in the system, such as performing
goods receipts against purchase orders, reporting daily production with scrap percent-
age, and recording the quality results of inspection lots.

17 Early Warning System
766

sections.title: Early Warning System in Action
sections.text:
17.4 Early Warning System in Action
For this example, the procurement supervisor creates a purchase order for material
QM003 and for supplier 17300006. The warehouse supervisor receives the partial pur-
chase order quantity of 200 PC in the system. The next step is to perform a quality
inspection that includes the results recording and usage decision. The details recorded
in the usage decision for the rejected material form the basis of the EWS alert. Rejected
material QM003, in a quantity greater than 50 PC, causes EWS to alert the person who
set it up. For this example, the alert is sent as a popup, and an email is sent to your SAP
inbox.
To create a new purchase order, use Transaction ME21N (see Figure 17.9 1). Enter the
Material “QM003”, Plant “1710” (not shown), and Supplier “17300006”. Press (Enter).
Save the purchase order, and, for this example, the system generates purchase order
number 4500001818.
Figure 17.9 Purchase Order and Goods Receipt
The next step is to record goods receipt against the purchase order. For this, use Trans-
action MIGO. Enter purchase order number “4500001818”, and press (Enter). In the
Quantity field, enter the partial procurement quantity as “200” PC, and enter storage
location “171A” (not shown). Save the goods receipt for purchase order number
4500001818 by pressing (Ctrl)+(S) 2.
© 

767
17.4 Early Warning System in Action
On goods receipt, the system creates an inspection lot. Because this material (QM003)
will undergo quality inspection, first record results using Transaction QE01 against the
inspection lot.
Finally, the last step is to undertake a usage decision using Transaction QE11 and reject
the material by returning the entire quantity of 200 PC back to the supplier (see the
Return Posting field in Figure 17.10, in which you enter “200” PC). On return delivery,
the system opens a popup to ask for a Reason for Mvmt. (movement). A reason for
movement enables the quality controller to specify the reason for rejecting or return-
ing the material back to the supplier. Select 0001 to denote a defective material, enter a
short text, press (Enter), and then save the usage decision.
Figure 17.10 Return Delivery to Supplier for Defective Material
As soon as you save the usage decision and choose Back, the system issues a popup
message (see Figure 17.11) to alert you of the deviation (exception) that’s occurred.
Figure 17.11 Popup Alert Issued by EWS

17 Early Warning System
768
Figure 17.11 shows that an exception (deviation) has occurred: the quantity rejected for
material QM003 during the usage decision was greater than 50 PC, leading to the
(popup) alert. Notice that in the popup, the system brings up the same text, Suppliers’
Rejections, that we defined during the initial stages of setting up EWS.
The system also delivers the same exception message in the SAP inbox. You can use
Transaction SBWP to check your inbox for unread documents that contain EWS alerts
too. It’s not always possible to keep track of all the EWS popups, so it makes sense to go
to the SAP inbox periodically and attend to your alerts (see Figure 17.12).
Figure 17.12 SAP Inbox
Tips and Tricks
While maintaining scheduling to check for individual exceptions or exception group-
ing, make sure to eliminate duplication of information so that the system doesn’t pres-
ent the same information repeatedly—first in an individual exception and then in an
exception grouping. This is achieved by adopting a well-thought-out approach prior to
setting up EWS—for example, by making a list of all the important materials for which
you want to monitor parameters for deviations.

sections.title: Exception Analysis
sections.text:
17.5 Exception Analysis
Finally, we’ll show you how to analyze exceptions with EWS in the QM information sys-
tem. Although alert monitoring is certainly a valuable EWS tool to promptly alert you
about any deviations and exceptions, often you’re required to have detailed informa-
tion on the exceptions. Fortunately, EWS is supported by QM, which ensures that com-
prehensive details related to all exceptions are instantly available.
© 

769
17.5 Exception Analysis
Follow menu path Logistics  Logistics Controlling  QM Information System  Early
Warning System  Exception Analysis or use Transaction MCYL to get to the initial
screen for exception selection. For this example, enter Exception “Z015” for analysis
(see Figure 17.13).
Figure 17.13 Exception Analysis
Figure 17.14 Exception Analysis Report of EWS for Material QM003

17 Early Warning System
770
Choose Execute, and the system displays the selection parameter screen. Enter
“QM003” for the Material field. When you execute the exception analysis report by
pressing (F8) or choosing Execute (not shown), the system displays the results, as
shown in Figure 17.14.
This exception analysis shows the defined key figure with its data as separate columns.
Further, the color is red for the entire row of the Material column, as we originally
defined in Figure 17.5.
As with all standard analysis reports, you can go to the menu and choose More  Extras 
Inspection Lot Drilldown to view the inspection lot’s details and other key figures.

sections.title: Summary
sections.text:
17.6 Summary
This chapter explained how quickly and easily a business process owner in any relevant
area of work can set up EWS without any extensive functional or technical knowledge.
EWS alerts can be modified, deleted, or updated anytime, as deemed necessary to
reflect the business need.
The next chapter covers QM reporting in the SAP S/4HANA system.
